note: 6 Nov 2026 - 'The Five Minute Phobia Cure | The Kevin Trudeau Show Limitless | Ep. 72' (Rumble v5xlxz8). Awakened Rise weekly agent. Most of this 60-minute show is a step-by-step self-therapy tutorial (tapping sequences, point-by-point instructions) - that is a treatment technique, not her lane, and never isolates cleanly from the instructions around it, so it was skipped. Four moments survive: the two teachings about WHY a fear exists (a past-life imprint, and 5,000-year-old Chinese organ/emotion mapping) that never slide into instructing the viewer, and two short personal stories (Archie's hidden fear of flying, the ice-cream craving) told briefly enough that the 'tap here' beat is a narrated aside, not a how-to.

clips.send: A friend who blames a phobia on one bad childhood memory, because this says it's older than that - awe, and a little unease.
clips.caption:
You didn't get this fear from falling in the water as a kid. According to Kevin, it didn't start in this lifetime at all.

He calls it a perturbation. Others call it an engram, or a samskar - an imprint carried into this body, sitting in your energetic field before you ever learned to be afraid of anything.

It shows up as contracted energy, blocking the flow through your meridians. That's the part nobody tells you: the fear was never really about the water, the spider, or the stage.

clips.caption:

Kevin learned it from Dr. Roger Callahan, the psychologist who built an entire technique out of one point under the eye - the one that reaches your stomach.

It's why 'it's sitting in my stomach' was never just an expression. Your body has been keeping score this whole time, in a language older than any of us.

clips.send: Someone who always has a reason not to fly, because this shows the 'quirk' is a nameable fear - and probably fixable in minutes.
clips.caption:
Archie wouldn't fly. Ever. So when Kevin invited him on a fishing trip in Canada, Archie just... drove. Three days, alone, rather than say the real reason.

Kevin finally got it out of him on the dock: he was petrified of flying, and had been his whole life. So Kevin sat him down on a plane that wasn't even running yet - no pilot, no engine, nowhere to go - and worked through the same sequence used on phobias and addictions.

A few minutes later, color back in his face, hand finally off the armrest, Archie looked up and asked what kind of magic that was. He flew everywhere after that. Never came back.

clips.send: A friend who's 'tried everything' to quit a food or habit, because this shows the craving itself can be erased, not just resisted - relief bordering on disbelief.
clips.caption:
She was addicted to one specific pint of ice cream - not any flavor, that exact one, every single day. She called it what it was: an addiction, like a drug.

Kevin put the open pint in front of her at a ten-out-of-ten craving and ran one thirty-second sequence. Not willpower. Not a trick to distract her. Just the craving itself, gone.

She picked the ice cream back up to test it - smelled it, imagined the taste - and felt nothing. Zero. It never came back, and six months later she called to tell him so herself.

Comment RISE and I'll send you how a craving actually gets erased.
